fixes.explanation: Nope, friend, nobody gets left at the gate on this one. Moses lists “…the foreigners in your camps who cut your wood and draw your water…” right there with the leaders and elders. They're standing before the LORD so that they may enter into the covenant (Deuteronomy 29:11–12). I know a thing or two about being the one in the back doing the work, and here they're front and center.

Baker, you caught it! The woodcutters and water carriers aren't left out at all. Moses puts “…the foreigners in your camps who cut your wood and draw your water…” in the very same lineup as the tribal leaders and elders. Everybody on that list is standing there so they may enter into the covenant (Deuteronomy 29:12). The people hauling the water get a seat, too.

That's right, friend! Moses reminds them, “You saw the abominations and idols among them made of wood and stone, of silver and gold.” They'd walked right past those nations on the way here, so they'd seen every bit of it (Deuteronomy 29:16–17). Silver and gold on the outside, and still just something somebody made by hand. I've been a thing somebody made by hand, too, and I know where I'd rather be put to work.
